financial_summary: GREATLAND RES LTD. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $4.5B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +147% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +5.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 70% against a 10% cost of capital — a 60-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 63% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $538M in free cash flow — roughly 35 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 0.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 19% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
